title: llm-routing-prefetch-prd-rough-scratchpad
summary: Scratchpad for a rough PRD exploring intelligent request routing + KV prefetching to reduce token costs and tail latency for multi-tenant hosted inference.
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad / rough PRD for an idea that came up during sprint planning and a follow-up sync with SRE and Applied ML. The goal: combine routing policies with predictive KV prefetching to (a) reduce per-token compute by reusing cached prefixes, (b) reduce 95/99th percentile latency for long conversational sessions, and (c) keep cost neutral or better via better batching and cache hit rates.

Problem statement:
- Many customer workloads have conversational sessions with repeated prompts, templates, or structured system messages. Right now we rely on reactive KV cache (server-side cache keyed by model+prefix).
- Cold starts and cache misses are a major driver for tail latency and token cost. Misses cause repeated decoding and GPU work for identical prefixes across tenants.
- Current routing is mostly static: route by region, model, or capacity tier. No routing signals to prefer nodes with warm KV for a specific tenant or prompt pattern.

Hypothesis:
If we route requests (or warm KV caches proactively) based on session patterns and lightweight prediction of next-prefixes, we can increase prefix cache hit rate significantly, improving latency and lowering unit cost by 10-30% for eligible workloads.

High-level approach / features (MVP):
1) Runtime telemetry collection (non-PII): track anonymized prefix fingerprints (hashed), frequency per tenant, and TTLs.
2) Offline analysis job to identify top-N prefixes per tenant/workload that would be worth prefetching.
3) Routing policy extension: allow route affinity to nodes/pools that already have a warm cache for tenant X or prefix fingerprint Y.
4) Proactive prefetch worker: when a session shows pattern matches, schedule async prefetch into a small pool to warm KV prior to expected calls.
5) Feature flags + opt-in: start with a small percent of traffic and only for customers who opt-in to allow prefetching.

User stories:
- As an ML engineer, I want the platform to reduce 95th percentile latency for interactive chat models so my end-users get snappier responses.
- As a platform operator, I want routing policies that take cache locality into account so we reduce redundant GPU work.
- As a security/compliance engineer, I want prefetching to avoid storing sensitive context and to respect KMS/tenant isolation.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Implement prefix fingerprinting pipeline and a dashboard showing top prefixes per tenant.
- Implement routing affinity that can route traffic to nodes with matching prefix fingerprints.
- Implement a simple prefetch worker that can load KV for top-10 prefixes per tenant into a designated warm pool.
- Demonstrate a 10% improvement in cache hit rate and 7% reduction in avg token cost for pilot tenants after 2 weeks.
- No customer PII or plaintext prompt storage; only hashed fingerprints and telemetry.

Technical considerations / constraints:
- Telemetry needs to be hashed/obfuscated before storage. We must get sign-off from security.
- Memory trade-offs: we will increase KV memory footprint on warm pools; need quota and eviction policy (LRU-ish per-tenant quotas).
- Prefetch timing: avoid unnecessary prefetches that increase GPU time without improving cache hit rate. Use conservative thresholds (min frequency and recency).
- Routing latency: affinity-based routing should not increase RTT; prefer local load-balancing with hints rather than global re-routing across regions.
- Compatibility: must work with quantized models and different KV layouts (decoder-only, chat, etc.).

Metrics to measure:
- Prefix cache hit rate (global, per-tenant)
- 50/95/99 latency for generation responses
- GPU-token cost and tokens-per-second per node
- Additional memory used by warm pools and eviction churn
- False positive prefetch rate (prefetches that were not used within TTL)

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: instrumentation + hashed-prefix collection pilot on internal traffic
- Week 3-6: offline analysis + dashboard; internal QA with synthetic workloads
- Week 7-10: deploy routing affinity + prefetch worker behind feature flag; opt-in pilot with 3 customers (low-risk)
- Week 11-14: expand to 20% traffic for eligible customers; monitor metrics and cost impact
- Post-mortem and iterate on thresholds/eviction policy

Open questions / risks:
- How to define prefix fingerprint granularity? (phrase-level vs token-window)
- Risk of increasing egress/GPU cost from prefetching too aggressively. Need budget controls per-customer.
- Multi-tenant warm pools could leak timing signals — ensure isolation and no cross-tenant contamination.
- Operational complexity: will SRE accept another routing signal? Can we keep it simple (per-pool header hints)?

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with Applied ML to define fingerprinting algorithm and hashing scheme (Priya + Aisha)
- Draft security checklist and get preliminary approval from security (Jordan)
- Spike: small PoC that computes hashed prefixes and measures repeat rate on 2 weeks of anonymized logs
- Create RFC stub for routing-affinity API and prefetch worker design (link to RFC-789)

Notes / random ideas to consider later:
- Combine with cost-aware routing: route to cheaper instances when cache hit predicted low and to warm expensive ones when hit predicted high.
- Offer customers an opt-out auto-eviction policy if they want deterministic memory usage.
- Expose "warm session" insights in Console: what prompts are being cached and estimated savings.

End of scratchpad.
